extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of natural philosophy, biology, astronomy, and physiology
extracted.subtask_short: analysis of equilibration in natural systems
extracted.subtask_description: A conceptual/theoretical exposition of the law of equilibration as it operates in physical (cosmical), biological (organismic), and mental systems; explains how aggregates evolve toward moving and complete equilibria and how structure and function adapt. Useful for readers studying comparative principles across astronomy, physics, physiology, and psychology.

rubrics_metrics.name: General law of equilibration
rubrics_metrics.description: The evolution of every aggregate must go on until this equilibrium mobile is established; an excess of force which the aggregate possesses in any direction must eventually be expended in overcoming resistances to change in that direction, leaving behind only those movements which compensate each other, and so form a moving equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equilibrium exists only when the arrangement of forces counterbalances all the forces to which the aggregate is subject; so long as there remains a residual force in any direction — whether exercised by the aggregate on the environment or vice versa — equilibrium does not exist and redistribution of matter must continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for absence of equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: So long as there remains a residual force in any direction ... equilibrium does not exist; and therefore the re-distribution of matter must continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence of any un-counterbalanced force or ongoing redistribution of matter/motion as diagnostic of nonequilibrium; only when forces are equalized does redistribution cease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of heterogeneity (structural specialization)
rubrics_metrics.description: The limit of heterogeneity towards which every aggregate progresses, is the formation of as many specializations and combinations of parts, as there are specialized and combined forces to be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicts structural complexity: an aggregate evolves additional specialized parts/functions up to the number required to counteract distinct external forces; structural complexity corresponds to the number, directions, and amounts of incident forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages of moving equilibrium in cosmical evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Those successively changed forms ... were so many transitional kinds of moving equilibrium; severally giving place to more permanent kinds on the way towards complete equilibration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: condensing nebulous matter assumes an oblate spheroidal figure (temporary moving equilibrium); formation/detachment of nebulous rings occurs when centrifugal force equals aggregative force for equatorial portion; rings then progress toward further equilibration (break up and concentrate into planetary bodies). Use matching of counteracting forces (centrifugal vs aggregative) to identify transitional equilibria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency of planetary motions toward complete equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: The moving equilibrium ... tends, in the course of indefinite time, to lapse into a complete equilibrium, by the gradual decrease of planetary motions and eventual integration of all the separate masses composing the Solar System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observational indicators include cometary retardations (e.g., Encke's comet) suggesting resistance and loss of momentum. Even if effects are infinitesimal over human timescales, the principle predicts ultimate reduction of planetary motions absent other sustaining mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibration of heat and conservation of force (solar cooling)
rubrics_metrics.description: The force known to us in solar radiations, is the changed form of some other force of which the Sun is the seat; by the gradual dissipation of these radiations into space, this other force is being slowly exhausted ... the Sun is gradually losing his heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument from persistence of force: radiation is transformed sensible motion; as concentration proceeds, heat generated is radiated away leaving only a diminishing internal remnant. Quantitative estimates (e.g., Helmholtz) are approximations but do not undermine the qualitative conclusion that the Sun's reserve of force is being expended and will be exhausted in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibrium figure of gravitating aggregates
rubrics_metrics.description: A spherical figure is the one which can alone equilibrate the forces of mutually-gravitating atoms. If the aggregate has rotatory motion, the equilibrium becomes a spheroid of greater or less oblateness according to the rate of rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply: measure centrifugal effects against gravitational aggregation to predict departure from sphericity (e.g., Earth's oblate spheroid counterbalances centrifugal force from axial rotation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent moving equilibria in terrestrial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The winds and waves and streams ... in their totality ... constitute a dependent moving equilibrium. There is traceable throughout them an involved combination of rhythms ... which, in the midst of irregularities, maintain an average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equilibrations are continuously renewed by external supply (Sun's power) while being dissipated; as solar input diminishes, sensible terrestrial motions and redistributions of matter will correspondingly decrease and eventually cease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-fold equilibration in living bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Every living body exhibits, in a four-fold form, the process we are tracing — in the balancing of mechanical forces (moment-to-moment); in the balancing of functions (hour-to-hour); in changes of state compensating changes of condition (year-to-year); and finally in the complete arrest of vital movements at death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organismic functions form a dependent moving equilibrium where motive power is dissipated and renewed (food supplies latent motion). Rhythmic processes maintain a constant mean and re-establish it when accidental causes cause divergence; extreme disturbances may establish a new mean (chronic change) or culminate in death (complete equilibration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation as equilibration around a new mean
rubrics_metrics.description: When through a change of habit or circumstance, an organism is permanently subject to some new influence ... there arises, after disturbance, a balancing of [organic rhythms] around the new average condition produced by this additional influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptation occurs via genesis of opposing permanent divergences (e.g., increased muscle use → increased nutrition → growth until balance between daily waste and repair). Structural changes (organs/sizes, connections) are the correlative of newly required functions; thus adaptation = equilibration manifested structurally and functionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-level equilibria (species numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every species ... is perpetually undergoing a rhythmical variation in number ... there is thus maintained an equilibrium between the sum of those forces which result in the increase of each race, and the sum of those forces which result in its decrease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oscillations of abundance and scarcity reflect compensating forces (food availability, enemies). The average population is the point where expansive tendencies are balanced by repressive tendencies; these oscillations and balancing must continue as part of ongoing equilibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibration in nervous and mental life
rubrics_metrics.description: The equilibrations of those nervous actions which constitute mental life ... Each pulse of nervous force ... is met by counteracting forces; sensations and emotions are expended in working bodily changes ... mental rhythms exhibit balancing of opposing forces at each extreme, and the maintenance of a general balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mental activity shows momentary, hourly/daily rhythms (activity/rest), desires equilibrated by expenditure or imagination (satiety), and intense passions balanced by counteracting forces leading to return to moderate excitement or a new medium state. Formation of mental connections corresponds to repeated external relations (ease of association proportional to repetition). Use resistance to thought, rhythmical alternation, and correspondence to external relations as markers of mental equilibration.
